one_liner: Embedded (in-process) C++ vector database with HNSW and int8 quantization; about 2x Zilliz Cloud QPS at matched recall in its own VectorDBBench run.
what_it_does: Zvec is a vector database that runs inside the application process: a collection is a directory on disk with a write-ahead log, scalar fields, dense and sparse vector fields and their indexes (flat, HNSW, HNSW-RaBitQ, IVF, IVF-RaBitQ, DiskANN/Vamana). The API is create_and_open / insert / query with a VectorQuery plus optional filter expression and full-text conditions, exposed through C++ and C libraries and Python, Node.js, Go, Rust and Dart SDKs. It is not a drop-in for Milvus: there is no server, no wire protocol and no distribution, so it replaces a vector-search service only when one process (or several read-only processes) can own the data.
how_it_is_fast: Search is HNSW (the parameter keys are still named proxima.hnsw.*, consistent with Alibaba's Proxima engine as its origin): a greedy descent through the upper layers, then a beam search on level 0. On current main the level-0 loop has a specialised fast path for mmap-backed contiguous storage that collects all unvisited neighbours, software-prefetches their vectors (by default every cache line of each vector), scores them with one batched SIMD distance call and keeps candidates in an AVX2 BlockHeap or a linear pool instead of the classic two-heap scheme. The benchmarked setup adds int8 scalar quantization (only the quantized vectors are held in memory, fp32 originals stay on disk) and an optional refiner that re-scores the ef candidates against the fp32 vectors; SIMD distance and quantizer kernels live in src/turbo with AVX2/AVX-512 paths. Running in-process removes the RPC, serialization and network hop that the client-server rivals pay per query. Note that the benchmark ran v0.1.1, so not every one of these main-branch paths was in the measured build.
when_to_use: An application (Python, Node.js, Go, Rust, Dart or C++) that needs local approximate nearest-neighbour search over up to roughly 10M 768-dimensional embeddings on one machine, without operating a Milvus or Qdrant server.
Local-first RAG, agent memory or code search where vectors, scalar filters and keyword full-text search must be combined in one query against one on-disk collection.
Read-heavy serving in which several worker processes query the same collection read-only (mmap) while one process does the writes.
You can accept recall@100 around 0.92-0.93 from int8 HNSW in exchange for throughput, or can afford fp32/refiner settings and tune ef upward for higher recall.
Edge or mobile deployments: since v0.7.0 releases ship prebuilt SDK binaries for Linux (glibc and musl), macOS, Windows, Android and iOS.
when_not_to_use: You need a distributed, replicated or multi-writer service; Zvec is single-node, and writes to a collection are exclusive to one process.
You need the recall levels of the Milvus HNSW rows (about 0.98): the published configuration reached 0.933 (10M) and 0.916 (1M), and no iso-recall curve against Milvus was published.

You only want a small ANN index library to vendor: Zvec pulls in Arrow, RocksDB, ANTLR, glog and a dozen other submodules; FAISS or hnswlib are leaner, and no Zvec-versus-FAISS/hnswlib numbers exist (issue #159 is open and deferred).

ARM64 with INT8 flat search, where INT8 was reported 2.3-4x slower than FP32 on Apple Silicon (issue #719, open), or AVX2-only x86 CPUs on early wheels (v0.1.1 crashed with SIGILL on Broadwell, issue #92).
You need a long-stable API and storage format: the project is v0.x (0.1.1 in January 2026 to 0.7.0 in August 2026) with recent concurrency crash fixes.

integration.form: shared lib (C++ and C APIs: zvec_shared, zvec_core_shared, zvec_ailego_shared; static targets for Android/iOS) or language SDK (PyPI wheel, npm, Go, Rust crate zvec-rust, Dart/Flutter)
integration.dependencies: vendored submodules: Apache Arrow, RocksDB, ANTLR, glog, gflags, CRoaring, FastPFOR, RaBitQ-Library, lz4, yaml-cpp, cppjieba, snowball, utf8proc, sparsehash, magic_enum, limonp (plus googletest for tests)
integration.min_toolchain: C++17, CMake >=3.26 and <4.0; Windows builds tested with MSVC 2022 only; Python wheels for 64-bit Python 3.10-3.14 per the README
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 and ARM64 (glibc and musl), macOS ARM64 and x86-64, Windows x86-64; v0.1.1 (the benchmarked release) shipped only manylinux x86-64 and macOS arm64 wheels, and its x86-64 wheel assumed AVX-512
integration.thread_safety: Multiple processes may open one collection read-only at the same time; writes are single-process exclusive. Within a process, concurrent query/fetch alongside insert crashed (SIGSEGV) when the writer crossed a segment switch until the fix for issue #714 (closed 2026-09-10); the query thread count is set once through init() at startup.

gotchas: Harness asymmetry: VectorDBBench ran Zvec in-process, with 12-20 spawned Python processes each opening the collection read-only through mmap on the same 16 vCPU g9i.4xlarge (Intel Granite Rapids according to a search snippet; the docs name no CPU), while the Milvus and Zilliz Cloud rows are Zilliz's stored client-server results from Xeon Platinum 8375C (Ice Lake) hosts. Hardware generation, deployment model and network hop all differ, so the ratios are not engine-versus-engine.

The 19x and 47x Milvus ratios are not iso-recall (Zvec 0.933 vs Milvus sq8 0.951 and Milvus HNSW 0.984 on 10M); only Zilliz Cloud 8cu matches recall, at about 2.1x (10M) and 1.7x (1M) QPS, derived from page data. The 10M run also used the fp32 refiner while the 1M run did not.

The benchmarked v0.1.1 int8 quantizer had a correctness bug: SQ8 sum/squared-sum metadata was computed from pre-rounded floats (issue #328, fixed by PR #329 on 2026-04-16). It cut recall on skewed data (OpenAI 1536D50K: 0.7377 before, 0.9588 after); maintainers reported no regression on Cohere 768D, and the bug lowers recall rather than inflating QPS, but the published numbers were measured on code later fixed in the quantizer hot path.

Quantization keeps both the fp32 and the quantized copy on disk, so storage grows; the refiner re-reads fp32 vectors, which needs them in page cache (about 31 GB for Cohere 10M, derived) to keep latency low.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No vector-search siblings are catalogued in this category: the siblings are ordered and learned key indexes (ALEX, PGM-index, LIPP, HOT) and embedded key-value stores (TidesDB, redb, libmdbx), none of which do nearest-neighbour search. Against FAISS (catalogued under autodiff-and-ml-kernels), pick Zvec when you want a persistent embedded database with WAL, filters, full-text search and multi-language SDKs rather than an in-memory index library; there are no head-to-head numbers.
verified_claims_summary: Alibaba's own VectorDBBench run of the zvec 0.1.1 PyPI wheel, in-process on a 16 vCPU / 64 GiB Alibaba g9i.4xlarge, using HNSW with int8 quantization (m=50, ef 118, fp32 refiner on Cohere 10M; m=15, ef 180 on Cohere 1M), reached 8,475 QPS (recall 0.933) on 10M and 16,490 QPS (recall 0.916) on 1M at concurrency 12-20. The rival rows are VectorDBBench's stored client-server results measured by Zilliz on Xeon Platinum 8375C hosts: Milvus 2.5.11 sq8 437 / 3,465 QPS, Milvus 2.2.12 HNSW 179 / 1,259 and Zilliz Cloud 8cu 3,957 / 9,704, so only the Zilliz Cloud comparison (about 2.1x and 1.7x, derived from page data) is at matched recall.
status_note: Actively developed (v0.7.0 on 2026-08-24, last commit 2026-09-29, 443 commits, 16.1k stars) and Apache-2.0, usable from C++ through shared libraries, but it is a young v0.x database with a heavy vendored dependency tree and recently fixed concurrency crashes (#714, #580), so pin a release and re-run VectorDBBench on your own hardware before relying on the published ratios.
